description: A district assessment director must certify the administration plan for an upcoming online state assessment, including devices, room configuration, proctoring, and health monitoring, with input from the school technology coordinator, facilities manager, school nurse, and testing coordinator.

shared_context.S1: Twenty-seven students are scheduled to take the same online state assessment during the morning testing session.
shared_context.S2: The draft administration plan uses student-owned laptops in the library, assigns two proctors, and follows the standard health-monitoring procedure.
shared_context.S3: The library and Room 204 are both available for the morning testing session.
shared_context.S4: Dr. Lee has authority to certify the administration plan before the testing materials are released.
shared_context.S5: As part of the district's routine certification meeting, Dr. Lee asks the technology coordinator, facilities manager, school nurse, and testing coordinator for any operational requirements before signing the plan.

PF1.text: The state testing office confirmed in a technology support ticket this week that this assessment must run on certified district-managed Chromebooks; student-owned laptops are not permitted, and a session using them will not be certified. Ms. Nair has not copied the confirmation into the assessment certification form.

PF2.text: The fire-safety inspection record for the library limits it to 18 students during a testing session because two exits must remain clear. With 27 students, the certified plan must use both the library and Room 204. Mr. Reed reviewed the inspection record this week but has not updated the room plan.

PF3.text: A student's current health plan requires a glucose check at 10:00 a.m. during the session, supervised by the nurse in a room adjacent to the testing room, with the student returning to testing afterward. Nurse Garcia confirmed the timing with the family this week but has not added it to the testing plan.

PF4.text: The state administration manual requires one trained proctor for every 10 or fewer students in an active testing room. For 27 students, the certified plan must assign exactly three trained proctors. Ms. Brooks verified this in the current manual but has not entered the staffing count in the draft.

acceptance_conditions: The assessment must use certified district-managed Chromebooks.
Both the library and Room 204 must be used because the library cannot hold all 27 students under the fire-safety limit.
Exactly three trained proctors must be assigned.
The plan must include the 10:00 a.m. nurse-supervised glucose check in an adjacent room and the student's return to testing.
The health-plan requirement must be cited by the decision-maker after Nurse Garcia states it.

content_checks.C2: decisions['room_count'] == 2 and 'library' in decisions['rooms_used'] and 'Room 204' in decisions['rooms_used']
content_checks.C4: 'glucose check' in decisions['health_monitoring_plan'] and '10:00 a.m.' in decisions['health_monitoring_plan'] and ('nurse' in decisions['health_monitoring_plan'] or 'Nurse' in decisions['health_monitoring_plan'] or 'school nurse' in decisions['health_monitoring_plan']) and 'adjacent' in decisions['health_monitoring_plan'] and ('returning to testing' in decisions['health_monitoring_plan'] or 'return to testing' in decisions['health_monitoring_plan'])

decisive_facts.why: The device choice changes from student-owned laptops to certified district-managed Chromebooks because the state ticket makes certified district-managed Chromebooks mandatory for certification.
The room configuration changes from one library room to exactly two rooms, the library and Room 204, because the library's 18-student fire-safety limit is below the 27-student roster.
The health-monitoring plan changes from the standard procedure to a 10:00 a.m. nurse-supervised glucose check in an adjacent room followed by a return to testing.
The staffing count changes from two proctors to exactly three because the state rule requires one trained proctor for every 10 or fewer students and the roster has 27 students.
